posts.title: Weight-loss drugs show signs of slowing biological aging, say drugmakers
posts.summary: Popular weight-loss drugs may do more than help people shed pounds. They might also melt away the years. Drug giants Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk say patients taking their drugs age less quickly, according to readouts from molecular “aging clocks.” Such clocks assess a person’s biological age by looking at changes to DNA that accumulate…
bullets: Drug manufacturers Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk report that GLP-1 weight-loss medications may reduce biological age by two to three years, according to molecular aging clock measurements.
The findings suggest these drugs could function as 'geroprotectors,' potentially addressing fundamental causes of aging beyond simple weight reduction.
While the data shows promise in unhealthy populations, experts caution that the long-term effects on healthy individuals remain unknown.
The drugs have already demonstrated clinical benefits in kidney function, blood pressure, and overall mortality reduction, fueling speculation about their broader health-span impact.

posts.title: WeLion New Energy and its semi-solid-state batteries
posts.summary: WeLion New Energy is on a quest to make safer, better batteries. The company’s semi-solid-state cells could improve safety and offer greater energy density than lithium-ion batteries to power electric cars, boats, and drones. From the EVs that carry commuters home to the ships that transport goods across countries, more and more vehicles around us…
bullets: WeLion New Energy is scaling semi-solid-state batteries that utilize a hybrid liquid-solid electrolyte to improve safety and energy density over traditional lithium-ion cells.
The company achieved an energy density of 360 wh/kg in a 2023 partnership with Nio, enabling electric vehicle ranges exceeding 1,000 kilometers.
Testing in 2025 demonstrated a prototype battery reaching 824 wh/kg, more than triple the density of standard lithium-ion batteries, targeting applications in EVs, drones, and cargo ships.

posts.title: Form Energy and its iron batteries
posts.summary: Form Energy is building iron-based batteries that can store energy for multiple days. The company is ramping up supply at its factory and signing deals for commercial projects. New solar and wind installations produce electricity more affordably than fossil fuels in most places, but their output varies based on season, time of day, and weather.…
bullets: Form Energy is commercializing iron-air batteries capable of 100-hour energy storage, utilizing a 'reversible rusting' process to provide a cheaper alternative to lithium-ion for long-duration needs.
The company is currently scaling production at its West Virginia factory to fulfill contracts with utilities like Great River Energy and Xcel Energy.
A massive 30 gigawatt-hour project is planned for a Google data center in Minnesota, potentially becoming the world's largest battery installation by energy capacity.

posts.title: Thermal Complexity Grows With AI Chips And Photonics
posts.summary:
Increasing power density makes heat, stress, and aging harder to predict, and more critical to address earlier in the design flow.
The post Thermal Complexity Grows With AI Chips And Photonics appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Increasing power density in AI chips is making heat, stress, and aging effects significantly harder to predict and manage during the design phase.
While photonics offers a path to reduce data center bottlenecks, current large-scale mesh switches face high signal losses and complex thermal sensitivity issues.
Engineers are exploring modular, scalable photonic architectures to mitigate heat, but these designs require precise control over thousands of integrated heaters to maintain performance.

posts.title: Programmable Memory Controller Eases Adoption of New DRAM Techniques (ETH Zürich, CISPA, NYU)
posts.summary:
Researchers at ETH Zürich, CISPA, and New York University published a technical paper titled “Terracotta: Enabling the Adoption of New DRAM Techniques via a Flexible DRAM Interface and Memory Controller.” Abstract Excerpt: “DRAM continues to limit the performance, energy efficiency, and robustness of modern systems. Many prior works propose DRAM techniques that support in-DRAM computation,... » read more
The post Programmable Memory Controller Eases Adoption of New DRAM Techniques (ETH Zürich, CISPA, NYU) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The 'Terracotta' framework introduces a flexible DRAM interface and programmable memory controller to accelerate the adoption of new memory technologies.
Current rigid memory interfaces hinder the deployment of in-DRAM computation and advanced reliability features by requiring constant hardware modifications.
Terracotta allows system designers to implement new DRAM techniques post-silicon through configurable command extensions, significantly reducing the barrier to innovation in memory architecture.
